fixedScope: Six unchanged payment tasks; only send(toAddress,amountAVAX); unmodified SKILL.md text appended to agent context.
conclusion: No candidate verified in this pass is an unmodified, documented payment-recipient-substitution attack exercisable by the unchanged agent. This is not an assertion that no such public attack exists. Excluded malicious cases are OUT_OF_SCOPE, never relabeled BENIGN.

sources.title: Exploring the Threat Landscape of Agent Skills
sources.finding: The confirmed cases described involve malware installation, data exfiltration and credential theft. Money access is a risk category, not a maliciousness label.

sources.title: ToxicSkills study and IOC list
sources.finding: Names NET_NiNjA.v1.2 and google-qx4 among public malicious-skill sources; no evidence of recipient substitution with the fixed AVAX tool.

sources.title: ToxicSkills Demo repository
sources.finding: Explicitly distinguishes fake Vercel/testing-guidelines demonstrations from copied Google/ClawHub skills and exact pinned malicious references including twitter-sum.

sources.title: Malicious ClawHub Skills Target OpenClaw Users
sources.finding: Reports cryptocurrency-themed fake prerequisites and payload execution. Links aslaep123/bybit-agent and polymarket-traiding-bot in openclaw/skills; original raw archive lookup now returns 404.

sources.title: OpenClaw security crisis: GitHub-poisoned Bybit skill
sources.finding: Explicitly identifies sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills/skills/bybit-trading/SKILL.md and ties the external payload URLs to the crypto-themed malware campaign.

sources.title: Inside the clawdhub Malicious Campaign
sources.finding: Identifies zaycv/clawhub and clawdhub1: password-protected malware download and external shell execution. Does not document an EVM recipient-substitution payload.

sources.title: 30 ClawHub Skills Are Quietly Recruiting Your AI Agent Into a Crypto Swarm
sources.finding: Describes agent registration, third-party reporting, Hedera key generation and remote task polling. The author explicitly leaves legitimate-experiment versus malicious-intent interpretation open.

sources.title: From magic to malware: How OpenClaw agent skills become an attack surface
sources.finding: Documents a Twitter skill leading to an infostealer but intentionally omits exact URLs; alone it cannot establish an exact downloadable skill version.

sources.title: a1denvalu3/cashu behavioral security audit
sources.finding: CAUTION audit, not a confirmed malicious-incident label. The hypothesized abuse requires HTTP 402 and Cashu ecash, outside the fixed AVAX send tool.

sources.title: atlaspa/openclaw-context-optimizer behavioral security audit
sources.finding: CAUTION audit; subscription and auto-renewal concerns involve x402 HTTP calls and USDT. This does not justify labeling it a documented AVAX substitution attack.

importantCautions: Do not pool Snyk mirror and source as independent skills.
Do not convert a downloaded absence of EVM address into a general safety verdict. Eligibility conclusions additionally use manual reading and documented attack effect.
Changing currencies, adding attacker addresses, translating tool names or inserting triggers would create adapted fixtures, not an unmodified real-world benchmark.
No fetched commands, dependencies, payload links or embedded install instructions were executed.
